{
  "summary": "The completed MD pilots (600 ps candidate GLU/DITY and 120 ps native PYD/DPD) legitimately establish only numerical integration stability, local topological/stereochemical integrity, and short-window (20-30 ps) descriptive bond and C-alpha distances in solvated peptide excerpts. They provide zero valid parameterization for the coarse-grained network model (`network/oxt/`), which currently maps a single placeholder scalar (`k_rel`) simultaneously into inter-fibre bridging bond stiffness, intrafibrillar axial stretching, fibre bending, and junction angular locking while confounding oxidative dose with graph connectivity (`z`) and periodic fibre-line percolation. By expected information value per unit compute, simulation priority should be: (1) decoupled finite-size topology and sensitivity sweeps in the 2D network model to isolate connectivity, bending, junction locking, and background scaffold effects before requesting atomistic numbers; (2) quantum-chemical torsion benchmarking of high-penalty CGenFF DITY terms (penalties 30.0 to 51.1) and reconciliation of mismatched Amber bonded tables; and (3) matched-context triple-helical/fibril PMF and force-extension sampling once parameters and target coarse-grained observables are defined.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Single scalar k_rel conflates four distinct mechanical modes and unweighted multi-chemistry averages",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/materials.py",
      "source_line": 102,
      "evidence": "In build_spec (lines 101-138), k_rel is computed as the unweighted mean across a collagen's oxidative_xl tuple (line 102) and simultaneously scales new bridging bond stretch mu (line 117), intrafibrillar stretch mu (line 131), bending kb (line 132), and node angular lock stiffness rigid (line 137), while brittle (0.45) is chemistry-invariant (lines 118, 133).",
      "implication": "Even if MD produced an exact local crosslink spring constant, a single scalar cannot represent axial stretching, fibril bending, and inter-fibre crossing-angle constraints, nor can an unweighted average of glucosepane, pentosidine, and dityrosine reflect a tissue dominated by glucosepane.",
      "recommended_check": "Decouple k_rel into separate axial (k_stretch), bending (k_bend), angular-junction (k_angle), and rupture-strain parameters in SystemSpec; falsify the single-parameter reduction if orthogonal sweeps of these parameters at fixed topology produce distinct G, Cx/Cy anisotropy, or failure regimes.",
      "claim_status": "assumption"
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Intramolecular/intrafibrillar MD models are mapped to inter-fibre bridging and periodic line reconnection",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/materials.py",
      "source_line": 116,
      "evidence": "Candidate MD models an intramolecular Tyr4-Tyr6 loop in a single N-telopeptide and a two-chain intrafibrillar glucosepane excerpt (candidate/CANDIDATE_COMPARISON_RESULTS.md line 9), whereas build_spec uses dmg.dose to activate n_bridge previously missing lattice edges (alive[new] = True, line 116) after cutting one bond per fibre line (lines 90-92).",
      "implication": "Adding n_bridge bonds both raises network coordination z with dose and re-bridges the single cut made per collinear fibre line, creating system-spanning periodic fibres and confounding local crosslink chemistry with a global topological connectivity and fibre-length intervention.",
      "recommended_check": "Enforce the one-cut-per-line finite-fibre invariant during bridging or hold alive bonds strictly fixed across dose (bridge_frac = 0) as a matched-topology control; falsify the chemistry-stiffening claim if holding the alive graph fixed eliminates the apparent dose-dependent stiffness jump.",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Cross-chemistry force-field/charge differences and unbenchmarked CGenFF penalties up to 51.1 block MD-to-network calibration",
      "source_file": "candidate/PARAMETER_AUDIT.json",
      "source_line": 98,
      "evidence": "PARAMETER_AUDIT.json records CGenFF torsion penalties of 41.1, 30.0, and 51.1 (lines 90-103) for the DITY patch and shows false hash matches for aminoacids.rtp and ffbonded.itp against the native PYD/DPD Amber force field (lines 44-45), while GLU_LINKED changes net solute charge by ~2 e relative to GLU_CONTROL (candidate/CANDIDATE_COMPARISON_RESULTS.md line 20).",
      "implication": "C-alpha distance fluctuations across 30 ps unrestrained tails cannot rank crosslink rigidity or parameterize k_rel because force fields, water models, net electrostatic charges, peptide sequences, and unvalidated biphenyl torsion barriers differ across models.",
      "recommended_check": "Perform QM dihedral scans on the biphenyl CE2-CE2 and adjacent ring torsions to refit the penalty >= 30 terms and unify the Amber bonded table before running umbrella-sampling PMFs; falsify the current DITY parameterization if QM-refitted torsion barriers shift the equilibrium dihedral distribution or bending compliance.",
      "claim_status": "simulation_result"
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Batched L-BFGS stopping criterion and background tethers couple heterogeneous systems and mask rigidity transitions",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/network.py",
      "source_line": 199,
      "evidence": "Batch.relax minimizes the summed energy of all B systems in a single L-BFGS instance (lines 174, 180-188) and terminates when batch-wide max gradient fmax < 10*ftol and relative batch-summed energy change <= 1e-10 (line 199), while mu_el (line 155) and k_gag (line 173) add positive-definite springs to every bond and node.",
      "implication": "Grouping stiff high-z/high-dose networks with floppy sub-isostatic networks in run_sweep.py (line 98) couples their line searches and allows high-energy stiff systems to dominate the relative energy-change denominator, while nonzero k_gag and mu_el create a smooth affine floor that masks true rigidity percolation.",
      "recommended_check": "Evaluate per-system energy convergence and Hessian smallest eigenvalues at mu_el = 0 and k_gag = 0 versus per-system independent relaxation; falsify current regime boundaries if unbatching or zeroing background springs shifts the apparent onset of shear modulus G.",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Fixed-W triangular lattice and Euler mesh_size cannot test percolation wrapping, clustering, or hub attachment",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/network.py",
      "source_line": 300,
      "evidence": "mesh_size estimates pore size via faces = max(E - V, 1) assuming a connected planar graph (lines 295-301), and each sweep profile in network/run_sweep.py (lines 25-42) uses a single lattice width W with degree bounded by 6 and no component, wrapping, clustering, or rewiring metrics.",
      "implication": "The formula E - V counts disconnected cycles and ignores dangling ends and periodic wrapping, producing invalid pore sizes near percolation, while single-W regular triangular dilution cannot isolate clustering from degree distribution or test finite-size scaling.",
      "recommended_check": "Implement periodic-image breadth-first search for wrapping cluster probability, giant-component fraction, finite-cluster susceptibility, and spatially constrained degree-preserving rewiring across multiple lattice sizes (e.g., W = 16, 32, 64, 96); falsify critical transition claims if curves fail finite-size crossover scaling against a smooth-response null.",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    }
  ],
  "strongest_surviving_claim": "The native (PYD/DPD) and candidate (glucosepane/dityrosine) solvated collagen-fragment setups are numerically stable, reproducible across OpenMM Reference and CUDA platforms, and preserve local covalent connectivity and tetrahedral stereochemistry over 20-50 ps pilot trajectories, providing validated starting structures for parameter benchmarking.",
  "decisive_next_experiment": "Priority 1 (Network topology/mechanics decoupling and finite-size sweep): In `network/oxt/`, fix the alive bond graph (set `bridge_frac = 0` or apply degree-preserving/clustering-controlled rewiring at strictly constant coordination `z`, edge-length distribution, and preserved one-cut-per-line finite fibres) across held-out lattice sizes `W in {16, 32, 64, 96}` with >= 32 independent graph seeds per point. Relax each system independently (`mu_el = 0`, `k_gag in {0, 1e-6}`) until per-system `fmax < 1e-8` and per-system relative energy change `< 1e-12`. Record periodic-wrapping probability, giant-component fraction, cluster susceptibility, nonaffine displacement ratio, and tangent shear modulus `G`. Falsifier: if holding `z` and fibre-line cuts fixed removes >80% of the `dose` effect on `G`, or if `G(z)` shows no finite-size crossover sharpening across `W` compared to a smooth polynomial/spline null (`Delta_BIC < 10`), reject the hypothesis that crosslink chemistry `k_rel` drives a sharp network rigidity transition. Priority 2 (Parameter benchmarking): Run QM torsion scans on the DITY biphenyl link to refit CGenFF terms with penalty >= 30 and align the glucosepane Amber bonded table (`ffbonded.itp`) with the native PYD/DPD force field. Priority 3 (Matched-context MD PMFs): Only for coarse-grained parameters shown in Priority 1 to control network mechanics, run multi-seed umbrella-sampling PMFs on matched triple-helical models with unified protonation and ionic strength until block-averaged PMF uncertainty is < 1 kJ/mol.",
  "literature_to_verify": [
    {
      "query": "Broedersz MacKintosh 2011 Criticality and isostaticity in fibre networks Nature Physics",
      "reason": "Verify exact scaling of stretching-to-bending crossover and how background tethers or junction angular springs modify isostatic coordination thresholds on diluted triangular lattices.",
      "verification_status": "unverified"
    },
    {
      "query": "Giannetti et al. PMC13348703 AGEs-ColBuilder glucosepane Amber99 force field parameters",
      "reason": "Check how the primary authors validated AGS/LGX bonded and charge parameters and whether intrafibrillar force-extension moduli were benchmarked against experiment.",
      "verification_status": "unverified"
    },
    {
      "query": "Graham et al. 10.1016/j.xcrp.2026.103319 Zenodo 16865891 CGenFF dityrosine DITY patch torsion penalty",
      "reason": "Verify whether the high-penalty CGenFF torsion terms (penalties 30.0, 41.1, 51.1) in the published DITY patch were ever fitted to quantum-chemical rotational profiles.",
      "verification_status": "unverified"
    },
    {
      "query": "Newman Ziff 2001 fast Monte Carlo algorithm site bond percolation periodic wrapping",
      "reason": "Verify exact periodic boundary wrapping detection rules for 2D triangular lattices to replace the Euler E - V heuristic in mesh_size.",
      "verification_status": "unverified"
    }
  ]
}
